portainer.notes: Cycle-35 batch-57 (2026-08-21, CVE scan + ssrf_vector_analysis). NOT CLEAN -- and the previous four batches that called it clean were not wrong, the world moved. CVE-2026-72533 / GHSA-jxhm-qq8x-v4c6 was published 2026-08-18, CVSS 4.0 9.4, and its range >=2.40.0 <2.45.0 covers the running 2.44.0. Filed REM-212 CRITICAL. THERE IS NO PATCH: neither 2.45.0 nor 2.39.7 exists on the releases endpoint, the tags endpoint, or Docker Hub as of today; newest STS is 2.44.0 (2026-07-30), newest LTS 2.39.6 (2026-08-12). The bypass is a path-normalisation defect -- Portainer strips only two-component Docker API version prefixes (/v1.47/) while the daemon also accepts three-component ones (/v1.47.0/), leaving a residue that matches neither the handler map nor the admin-only route list, so BOTH authorization gates miss. Precondition is an authenticated NON-ADMIN, which this estate does produce: Authentik tier-1 gates who gets a session, but an OAuth-provisioned Portainer account is a standard user, not an administrator. MITIGATION MEASURED, not assumed: portainer runs --host tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375, and the LIVE proxy env has PLUGINS=0 (which independently neutralises the older CVE-2026-44848), ALLOW_START/STOP/RESTARTS=0, SECRETS=0, CONFIGS=0 -- but POST=1 and EXEC=1, so the bypass still reaches POST /containers/{id}/exec into any already-running container. Reduced from host RCE to broad in-container command execution; not closed. METHOD NOTE: OSV returned NINE portainer advisories for 2.44.0 and ALL NINE were false positives (Go introduced:0 range mapping; every one fixed at 2.33.8/2.39.2/2.41.0). The one real CRITICAL appears only on the vendor's GHSA endpoint. An OSV-only scan would have reported this component clean. RE-READ NEXT BATCH regardless of rotation -- an unpatched CRITICAL is what the 14-day drift window is too slow for. Prior probe REM-182 (CVE-2026-55761 uninitialised-instance takeover) remains correctly MITIGATED: the instance is initialised.

That is the evidentiary standard REM-144 explicitly could not meet (split-horizon dnsmasq had resolved its 'public' test back to the LAN, so it correctly refused to claim internet exposure); future probes should reach for --resolve against the authoritative public address before either claiming or disclaiming reach. It also overturns the 'pre-auth leg is CLOSED' disposition rustfs had carried since batch-36 -- the leg is not closed, it is narrowed to /health and /favicon.ico, and /health is the one that talks. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is about TIME rather than about headers: an advisory verdict is only true as of the hour it was read. REM-187 recorded rustfs's advisory leg clean at 04:12 and predicted, from this vendor's demonstrated habit of retroactively naming later releases as sole-patched, that beta.11 would likely acquire advisories anyway. Six were published at 14:13 the same day -- four against beta.11 and two against beta.12, the very version REM-187 recommended bumping TO. The prediction was right within ten hours, which means for a no-CVE prerelease vendor a clean verdict must carry its timestamp and a short shelf life. Pair that with the version disclosure above and the two findings compose: the estate publishes, anonymously and worldwide, exactly the string an attacker needs to know when this host's version enters an affected range. SECONDARY PATTERN, the probe's nominal quarry across all five: the components with NO HTTP surface are not automatically silent. MariaDB's pre-auth MySQL handshake advertises '11.8.8-MariaDB-ubu2404' -- application version AND Ubuntu base image -- to anyone who can open a socket, which is protocol-inherent and unfixable by config; Redis under --requirepass answers '-NOAUTH Authentication required.' to INFO, PING and LOLWUT alike and discloses nothing, a protocol-design difference rather than a configuration one. And qgis_server returns `Server: Apache/2.4.18 (Ubuntu)` -- one header fingerprinting a 2019 Ubuntu 16.04 userland -- which is not a new row but is the cleanest possible evidence for REM-184; it does not reach the internet only because REM-185's missing Authentik Provider makes the edge 404 first. --- PRIOR: Cycle-17 batch-38 FIRST RUN of this probe type, over woodpecker/jellyfin/traefik/uptime_kuma/calibreweb (2026-07-30): 4 items (REM-144 CRITICAL, REM-145 HIGH, REM-146 LOW, REM-147 LOW) + REM-148. Lesson recorded there: 'oidc' means the edge is open and the app's own login is the only gate; 'none' means there is no gate at all. Also: security-headers@file strips NO response headers, it only adds, so any upstream Server or X-Powered-By passes through the edge untouched.

Cycle-39 batch-58 SECOND RUN of this probe type, over tileserver/traefik/woodpecker/jellyfin/uptime_kuma (2026-08-24). 4 items filed (REM-222 traefik MEDIUM, REM-223 tileserver MEDIUM, REM-224 uptime_kuma MEDIUM, REM-225 LOW gate coverage) + REM-146 (woodpecker) CLOSED by measurement.

THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD (REM-223): A VERSION NUMBER DOES NOT DESCRIBE THE ARTIFACT. tileserver-gl is at v5.6.0, which is the newest release that exists -- npm latest, zero advisories on the repo, the sole OSV entry fixed six years and two majors below the pin. Its version leg is permanently, correctly, unimprovably GREEN, and it will report green in every future cycle. Underneath it the container carries 56 pending Ubuntu -security updates including libc6, a libcurl four security revisions behind, and a ca-certificates trust store dated 20240203. There is no version to bump; the fix is an image rebuild nobody currently asks for. This is the previous run's lesson ('scanning versions answers is-the-number-old, never is-the-number-load-bearing') one turn further out: the number can be perfect and the artifact still stale, and no scanner in this estate looks inside (REM-225).

THE SECOND PATTERN, which is what makes the first actionable: IMAGE AGE DOES NOT PREDICT PACKAGE STALENESS -- BASE-DISTRO CHOICE DOES. Measured across all five, pending -security packages against image age: tileserver (Ubuntu 24.04, 140 days) 56; jellyfin (Debian 13 trixie, 79 days) 14; uptime-kuma (Debian 12 OLDSTABLE, 23 days) 11 but including Chromium three majors behind; traefik (Alpine 3.24, 24 days) 2, both apk-tools; woodpecker (scratch, 5 layers, no shell) 0 with no surface to accumulate on. The 23-day-old image is worse positioned than the 79-day-old one. So a freshness heuristic keyed on image age would have ranked these almost exactly backwards, and the useful question is not 'when was this built' but 'what is it built ON'.

THE THIRD PATTERN, on the CVE leg, and it retires a phrase this scanner has been using: 'OSV EMPTY' IS NOT A CLEAN VERDICT. Cycle-27 called traefik clean at v3.7.10 citing an empty OSV query, correctly, on 2026-08-12. Nine days later upstream published four advisories against exactly that version -- one of them CVSS v4 9.3, a complete authentication bypass in digestAuth -- and at scan time NOT ONE is in OSV, whose newest traefik record is 2026-08-18. Three of the four carry NO CVE ID. The measured OSV ingestion lag for this vendor is about twelve days. Worse, for Jellyfin the record will never arrive at all: api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/GHSA-wwwm-px48-fpvq returns nothing, because Jellyfin is not in an ecosystem OSV indexes, so its entire advisory corpus is invisible to the query this scanner leans on. Cycle-19/20 learned 'a GHSA with no CVE id'; the correction now goes one layer deeper -- the OSV MIRROR is not the vendor's advisory endpoint either, and for anything internet-facing the vendor's own /security/advisories page must be read directly.

FOURTH, ON EVIDENCE STANDARDS, because the scanner caught itself: the first base-layer measurement returned 0 upgradable for tileserver and would have been filed as CLEAN. It was false. The image runs as non-root, `apt-get update` failed with 'List directory /var/lib/apt/lists/partial is missing. - Acquire (13: Permission denied)', and the counting pipeline read the empty output of a failed command as an empty result -- CLAUDE.md's success-marker class occurring inside the security scanner itself. Every figure above comes from a re-run with --user 0 where the package manager exited 0. RULE FOR THIS PROBE TYPE: assert the package manager's exit status before counting its output.

FIFTH, A DELIBERATE COUNTER-EXAMPLE AND A MEASURED CLEAN. Registry Docker-Content-Digest was compared against the local RepoDigest for all six images, and all six match -- no tag has been re-pointed under the estate. That reproducibility is real but it is held by vendor good behaviour rather than by construction: nothing in the estate pins a digest for these five, and REM-224 documents a vendor that shipped three tags in 2h39m, one self-described as carrying the wrong version number. Recording the clean AS MEASURED is the point -- it is the evidence a future 'the tags are fine' assumption should have to beat.

Estate-wide: 0 of 52 role compose templates digest-pin, version_policy 'stable' renders --pull EMPTY at all five consumers so nothing ever re-pulls, and versions.json records zero digests -- meaning a content swap on a mutable tag could be neither prevented nor detected after the fact (REM-207). COVERAGE CEILING, stated rather than implied: this probe read registry metadata and repo/tag state. It did NOT verify image signatures or provenance attestations, did not diff layer contents against upstream build recipes, and did not audit the language-level dependency manifests inside any image. Absence of a finding on those axes is absence of a test, not evidence of cleanliness.

Probe produced ONE finding of its own class (REM-209, onlyoffice) plus one CVE-leg finding (REM-208, erpnext). The probe-class result: of five components, exactly one discloses its version to an anonymous caller at the edge, and it does so in the RESPONSE BODY while its Server header reads a bare 'nginx' -- /index.html and /web-apps/apps/api/documents/api.js both serve 'Version: 9.3.1'. A header-only probe of this class would have reported all five CLEAN and been wrong about one; read the body. The four measured-clean comparators are recorded in their component notes so the negative result is not re-derived: homeassistant blanks Server: to an empty string on every path, firefly returns bare 'nginx' and 302s anonymous callers to Authentik, ntfy emits no Server header and no version, erpnext is not running and was honestly marked NOT ASSESSABLE. Two corrections came out of the batch rather than the probe. (1) Home Assistant's CVE leg was declared clean by batch-43 while the estate ran a version affected by CVE-2026-64824 (Core < 2026.7.0, symlink path-traversal to root RCE via backup-restore); the CVE is absent from all 23 home-assistant/core repo advisories and present in the CVE feed and OSV, INVERTING batch-43's own 'query the vendor repo endpoint or see nothing' lesson. Both sources must be queried. (2) REM-167's Authentik mitigation for ntfy is falsified -- forward-auth was removed 2026-08-08 so phones could subscribe -- though its severity survives, since publish now requires a credential in ntfy's own user DB. Also established: four of the five components are LIVE despite every prior batch citing install_X=false, because config.yml overrides the default for ntfy, homeassistant, firefly and onlyoffice; only erpnext is genuinely absent.

Two of five components moved clean->affected in the 13 days since batch-46, and NEITHER move was visible to OSV -- portainer's nine OSV hits were all Go-range false positives while the real CRITICAL sat only on the vendor GHSA endpoint. Fourth recurrence of the scan-the-vendor-not-the-CVE-feed lesson. REM-212 is the queue's only pending CRITICAL and has NO released patch (2.45.0 / 2.39.7 do not exist); it needs re-reading next batch outside the normal rotation. Clean and honestly so: openwebui 0.11.0 sits at or above all 30 published fix lines, postgresql 16.14 IS the fix line for the newest PG cohort (16.15 exists but carries no security content -- a bare latest-vs-pin check would misfire), bluesky_pds has zero advisories across the pds repo, the atproto repo and four @atproto npm packages.

Second run of this probe (first was cycle-30 over bone/wing/pulse/miniflux/nodered -> REM-203). It produced one estate-wide finding and two component-level ones, and the estate-wide one is the finding of record: the estate declares mem_limit on 53 of 53 compose templates and 60 of 60 running containers, and declares pids_limit or ulimits on ZERO of either -- so it controls the two axes that are easy to reason about and neither of the two a fork bomb or fd exhaustion uses, against a Docker VM whose kernel.pid_max (99999) and fs.file-max (2,379,288) are shared by all 60 containers (REM-219). The same row records that the memory control it DOES have is not an aggregate one: 54.75 GiB of mem_limit committed against 22.7 GiB of VM, 241 per cent, or 482 with Docker's implicit 2x memswap. Component-level: FreeScout accepts a 2G upload into a 512m container with max_execution_time 0, where the memory leg is mitigated by nginx/PHP spooling to disk but the disk and worker-occupancy legs are not (REM-220); and not one of 41 live Traefik routers carries a rateLimit, inFlightReq or buffering middleware, which Outline currently survives only because outlinewiki ships its limiter on by default -- a control in the dependency rather than the deployment (REM-221). COVERAGE CEILING, stated rather than implied. TWO of the five components were NOT MEASURED: qgis_server and superset both resolve install=false and neither is in docker ps, so they got template review only -- a regression in coverage from batch-48/49, which measured both running. Their latent template hazards are named in their component notes and deliberately NOT filed as rows, because a service with no deployment has no exposure. For the three live services, NO EXHAUSTION WAS EXECUTED -- no fork storm, no memory balloon, no 2G upload, no connection flood was driven against the operator's live estate. Every figure is read from the Docker daemon's own accounting, the containers' own config files, and the rendered Traefik config. Also untested on every component: disk-quota exhaustion of the host bind mounts (headroom measured at 53 GiB of 460, consumption not attempted), PostgreSQL and Redis connection-pool exhaustion from a saturating client, and any exhaustion path through the Authentik outpost that gates three of these five routers.

attack_probes_completed.note: Probe produced ONE genuine SSRF-chain finding and three verdicts of mitigated-by-construction. The finding is REM-234: pulse's two-day-old `vouch()` credential pre-flight POSTs the agent client_secret with check_hostname=False AND CERT_NONE, which turns the still-pending REM-154 rebind relay from a DNS hygiene item into the first link of a credential-disclosure chain -- the probe's value this batch was joining two findings that were each individually parked. MITIGATED, with reasons recorded so they are not re-derived: alloy has NO steerable target (every __address__ a hardcoded localhost literal, no discovery.docker/relabel/file_sd); wing's WebhookDispatcher curl_init($url) is closed on both provenance (URLs composed internally by SubscriptionRegistrar, no HTTP route accepts one) and redirects (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION=false). THEORETICAL, documented not filed: bone's _check_health fans out with follow_redirects=True and verify=False, giving a blind port-scan oracle -- but it carries no credential and needs the nos:state:read scope, re-verified live (unauth aggregate -> 401).
